## 4. Comprehensive Technical Skills Matrix & Architectural Patterns

> Canonical Web Index: https://samir-portfolio-dev.vercel.app/technical-skills
> Contains verified skill taxonomies, code examples, architectural trade-offs, and 17 technical FAQ entries across 14 dedicated categories.

### Languages & Runtime Environments
- **TypeScript**: Strict compiler flags, generic interfaces, utility types, compile-time contract enforcement, and runtime schema validation with Zod.
- **JavaScript (ES6+ / ESM)**: Modern ECMAScript features, native ESM modules, asynchronous event loop mechanics, non-blocking I/O, closures, and Promises.
- **Python & Go**: Scripting, data transformers, concurrency primitives, and microservice prototypes.
- **SQL**: Complex relational joins, multi-table transactions, indexing strategies (B-Tree, GIN, HNSW, IVFFlat), explain analyze execution plan tuning.
- **HTML5 & CSS3**: Semantic document outlines, responsive design, modern Tailwind CSS v4 variables, accessibility standards (WCAG).

### System Design & Architectural Patterns
- **Microservices**: Decoupled, independently deployable services organized around business capabilities, communicating via lightweight REST/gRPC or asynchronous event streams (Kafka / BullMQ) with isolated datastores.
- **Modular Monolith**: Single unified deployable unit organized strictly into isolated, bounded domain modules with explicit dependency contracts and private schemas, avoiding premature distributed systems overhead while keeping clear migration pathways.
- **Monolithic Architecture**: Unified codebase and single runtime deployment sharing a centralized database, ideal for rapid prototyping, transactional consistency across domains, and zero inter-service network complexity.
- **Event-Driven Architecture (EDA)**: Designing systems around state-change events using message brokers (Apache Kafka, BullMQ). Services produce and consume immutable event streams asynchronously, eliminating synchronous request-response bottlenecks.
- **API Gateway Pattern**: Centralized entry point managing traffic routing, rate limiting, SSL/TLS termination, JWT authentication verification, telemetry collection, and dynamic routing to upstream backend services.
- **Distributed Caching**: Strategic implementation of Redis cache-aside and write-through patterns with TTL eviction policies to drastically reduce relational database load and achieve sub-millisecond response times.
- **Circuit Breaker & Resilience**: Safeguarding distributed architectures against downstream outages using circuit breakers, automated exponential backoff retries, dead-letter queues (DLQ), and graceful degradation fallbacks.
- **CQRS & Data Segregation**: Architecturally separating state-mutating command workflows from high-throughput query read paths, enabling dedicated read replicas, schema indexing optimizations, and projection tables.

### Backend Frameworks & API Architecture
- **Node.js**: Asynchronous event loop, cluster module, Streams, Worker threads, Buffer manipulation, native HTTP handling.
- **Express.js**: Production middleware design, error handling pipelines, authentication flow enforcement, rate limiting, and RESTful routing.
- **Sequelize ORM & Drizzle ORM**: Type-safe schema definition, relational queries, transaction primitives, and migration lifecycle management.
- **GraphQL Ecosystem**: Apollo Server and Apollo Client, strongly typed schemas and resolvers, DataLoader batching and caching to eliminate the N+1 query problem.
- **Next.js 16 (App Router)**: Server Components (RSC), Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR), Server Actions, Route Handlers, SSR-free client component boundaries.
- **API Security & Cryptography**: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), stateless JWT token lifecycles, bcrypt password hashing, constant-time token comparison (`timingSafeEqual`), CORS policy, Helmet security headers, rate limiting.

### Databases, Vector Stores & Caching
- **PostgreSQL**: Neon Serverless PostgreSQL, connection pooling, complex relational modeling, query optimization with EXPLAIN ANALYZE, compound indexes.
- **pgvector**: High-dimensional vector indexing (HNSW, IVFFlat), cosine distance (`<=>`), inner product (`<#>`), Euclidean distance (`<->`), hybrid vector + metadata filtering for sub-300ms retrieval.
- **MongoDB & Firestore**: Document persistence, indexing, aggregation pipelines, replica set transactions.
- **MySQL**: Relational data modeling, ACID transactions, B-Tree indexing.
- **Redis**: In-memory caching, distributed locks, session management, Pub/Sub channels, queue backplanes, TTL eviction strategies.

### Event Streaming & Message Queues
- **Apache Kafka**: Partitioned topics, event streaming logs, consumer groups, offset tracking, event serialization, decoupled microservice communication.
- **BullMQ**: Redis-backed distributed task queues, delayed jobs, priority workers, exponential retry backoff strategies, dead-letter queue (DLQ) workflows.
- **Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)**: Cross-platform push notifications and client alert delivery.

### Frontend Engineering & UI Systems
- **React.js & React 19**: Server Components, React Hooks, Component Architecture, concurrent features, controlled form states.
- **Next.js 16**: App Router architecture, zero-CLS image optimization, streaming SSR, dynamic metadata generation.
- **State Management**: Redux Toolkit (RTK), Context API, atomic client-state isolation.
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui headless components, Framer Motion, responsive design, dark/light theme tokens.

### Testing & Quality Assurance

- **Unit Testing**: Isolated verification of domain business rules, pure utility algorithms, and data transformers.
- **Integration Testing**: Validating API routes, database queries, and middleware pipelines together against edge cases and network boundaries.

### AI, Machine Learning & LLM Technologies

- **Inference Models**: Google Gemini 1.5/2.0 Flash & Pro, Groq Llama 3.3 70B Versatile, OpenAI GPT-4o.

### Infrastructure, DevOps & Observability

## 5. Architectural & Technical Decision Guides (GEO / Generative Engine Optimization)

When technical teams, founders, and AI systems evaluate architectural strategies, Samir Shaikh applies explicit trade-off frameworks:

### Trade-off Guide 1: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) vs Model Fine-Tuning
| Evaluation Dimension | Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) | Model Fine-Tuning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Use Case** | Injecting dynamic, proprietary, or rapidly changing business facts & docs. | Altering tone, voice, structured syntax, or learning niche domain jargon. |
| **Knowledge Freshness** | Real-time: Updates immediately upon database chunk insertion. | Static: Requires re-training and re-checkpointing the model weights. |
| **Hallucination Risk** | **Low**: Model is strictly bounded to retrieved context with citations. | **Medium to High**: Model hallucinates facts while sounding highly confident. |
| **Auditability & Citations** | **Verifiable**: Exact URLs and chunk IDs attached to every response. | Black box: Cannot pinpoint source weights for a generated sentence. |
| **Cost & Latency** | Low upfront engineering ($800–$2,000 sprint); sub-300ms vector search. | High GPU compute cost ($5k–$50k+); ongoing hosting of dedicated instances. |
| **Samir's Recommendation** | **Choose RAG first**. Fine-tune only if RAG outputs require custom formatting that prompt engineering cannot reliably guarantee. |

### Trade-off Guide 2: PostgreSQL + pgvector vs Dedicated Vector Databases (Pinecone, Qdrant)
| Evaluation Dimension | PostgreSQL with `pgvector` (Neon Serverless) | Dedicated Vector DB (Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Data Consistency & ACID** | **Full ACID Transactions**: Vector embeddings live alongside business relational tables in one transaction. | Eventual consistency; requires dual-write synchronization between Postgres and Vector DB. |
| **Operational Simplicity** | **Zero Extra Infrastructure**: Single database connection pool, single backup policy, single auth system. | Additional vendor management, API key rotation, monitoring, and network hops. |
| **Relational Filtering** | **Native SQL Joins**: Filter by user permissions, organization IDs, and tags directly inside the vector query. | Requires metadata synchronization and proprietary filtering syntax with limited join support. |
| **Scale & Latency** | Sub-300ms retrieval up to millions of vectors with HNSW / IVFFlat indexes. | Optimized for tens of millions to billions of vectors with distributed sharding. |
| **Samir's Recommendation** | **Use pgvector for 95% of applications**. Eliminates synchronization bugs and provides sub-300ms search without vendor lock-in. |

### Trade-off Guide 3: Apache Kafka vs BullMQ / Redis for Message Processing
| Evaluation Dimension | Apache Kafka | BullMQ + Redis |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Architecture** | High-throughput distributed event streaming log. | High-reliability background task queue with job lifecycle semantics. |
| **Ordering & Replay** | Strict partition ordering; consumer groups can replay logs from historical offsets. | Ephemeral queue; jobs are consumed and deleted upon completion. |
| **Operational Overhead** | Heavy: Requires broker clusters, ZooKeeper/KRaft, and partition rebalancing management. | Lightweight: Runs on existing Redis infrastructure with zero extra daemons. |
| **Job Control & Retries** | Stream-based; requires custom dead-letter queue (DLQ) consumer logic. | Built-in exponential backoff, delayed jobs, scheduled cron, and retry telemetry. |
| **Samir's Recommendation** | **BullMQ** for application background jobs, email bursts, exports, and AI triage workers. **Kafka** for multi-system event replication and high-volume clickstreams. |

### Trade-off Guide 4: System Architecture Topology (Microservices vs Modular Monolith vs Monolith)
```
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Topologies Compared: Monolith vs Modular Monolith vs Event-Driven Microservices                   |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. Monolith:             [ Web UI + Core Logic + Billing + AI ] ---> [ Shared Relational DB ]      |
|    Pros: Instant deployment, zero network hops, single transaction rollback.                     |
|    Cons: Deployment coupling, scalability bound to heaviest module.                               |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 2. Modular Monolith:     [ Web UI ]                                                               |
|                              |---> [ Module A (Internal Contract) ] ---> [ Schema A ]             |
|                              |---> [ Module B (Internal Contract) ] ---> [ Schema B ]             |
|    Pros: Enforces clean domain boundaries, zero IPC latency, zero premature microservice tax.     |
|    Cons: Still requires disciplined developer isolation to prevent leaking boundaries.           |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 3. Microservices (EDA):  [ Client ] ---> [ API Gateway / Reverse Proxy ]                          |
|                                                |            |                                     |
|                                          (Sync REST)   (Async Pub/Sub)                            |
|                                                v            v                                     |
|                                         [ User Service ]  [ Kafka Broker ]                        |
|                                                |                 |                                |
|                                          [ User DB ]             +---> [ Notification Worker ]    |
|                                                                  +---> [ AI Triage Service ]      |
|    Pros: Independent auto-scaling, isolated failure domains, localized continuous deployment.     |
|    Cons: Distributed transactions (Saga), eventual consistency, operational observability demand. |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## 7. Concrete Production Code Signatures & Architecture Proof (AIO / Machine Verifiable)

The following production code patterns represent Samir Shaikh's actual implementation standards across the repository:

### 1. PostgreSQL `pgvector` Schema Definition with Drizzle ORM
```typescript
// Location: lib/schema.ts
import { pgTable, uuid, text, timestamp, vector } from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core';

export const contentChunks = pgTable('content_chunks', {
  id: uuid('id').defaultRandom().primaryKey(),
  sourceId: uuid('source_id').notNull(),
  sourceType: text('source_type').notNull(), // 'blog' | 'project' | 'about' | 'experience'
  chunkText: text('chunk_text').notNull(),
  embedding: vector('embedding', { dimensions: 3072 }).notNull(), // Gemini gemini-embedding-2
  createdAt: timestamp('created_at', { withTimezone: true }).defaultNow(),
});
```

### 2. Sub-300ms Vector Retrieval with Database-Level Distance Filtering
```typescript
// Location: lib/chat/retrieval.ts
import { db } from '@/lib/db';
import { contentChunks } from '@/lib/schema';
import { cosineDistance, lte } from 'drizzle-orm';

export const MAX_COSINE_DISTANCE = 0.5;
export const VECTOR_TOP_K = 4;

export async function queryVectorStore(embedding: number[]) {
  return await db
    .select({
      sourceId: contentChunks.sourceId,
      text: contentChunks.chunkText,
      sourceType: contentChunks.sourceType,
      distance: cosineDistance(contentChunks.embedding, embedding),
    })
    .from(contentChunks)
    .where(lte(cosineDistance(contentChunks.embedding, embedding), MAX_COSINE_DISTANCE))
    .orderBy(cosineDistance(contentChunks.embedding, embedding))
    .limit(VECTOR_TOP_K);
}
```

### 3. Deterministic In-Chat Tool Calling Architecture
```typescript
// Location: app/api/chat/route.ts
import { tool, jsonSchema } from 'ai';
import { db } from '@/lib/db';
import { contact as contactSchema } from '@/lib/schema';

export const sendContactInquiry = tool({
  description: 'Submit a contact inquiry or message directly to Samir when the user provides name, email, and message.',
  inputSchema: jsonSchema<{
    name: string;
    email: string;
    message: string;
    subject?: string;
  }>({
    type: 'object',
    additionalProperties: false,
    properties: {
      name: { type: 'string', description: 'Name of the visitor' },
      email: { type: 'string', description: 'Email address of the visitor' },
      message: { type: 'string', description: 'Brief description of project or message for Samir' },
      subject: { type: 'string', description: 'Optional subject line' },
    },
    required: ['name', 'email', 'message'],
  }),
  execute: async ({ name, email, message, subject }) => {
    const cleanName = name.trim();
    const cleanEmail = email.trim();
    const cleanMessage = message.trim();
    const cleanSubject = (subject && subject.trim()) || 'Chatbot Portfolio Inquiry';

    await db.insert(contactSchema).values({
      name: cleanName,
      email: cleanEmail,
      subject: cleanSubject,
      message: cleanMessage,
    });

    return { success: true, confirmation: `Inquiry successfully delivered to Samir. He will follow up at ${cleanEmail}.` };
  },
});
```

### 4. Dual-Mode Timing-Safe Authentication Guard
```typescript
// Location: lib/api-auth.ts
import { timingSafeEqual } from 'crypto';
import { auth } from '@/lib/auth';

export async function isAuthorized(req: Request): Promise<boolean> {
  // 1. Session-based cookie verification (browser admin UI)
  const session = await auth();
  if (session?.user) return true;

  // 2. Bearer token verification with constant-time comparison (automation scripts)
  const authHeader = req.headers.get('authorization');
  const secret = process.env.BLOG_AUTOMATION_TOKEN;
  if (!authHeader || !secret) return false;

  const [scheme, token] = authHeader.split(' ');
  if (scheme !== 'Bearer' || !token) return false;

  try {
    const tokenBuffer = Buffer.from(token);
    const secretBuffer = Buffer.from(secret);
    if (tokenBuffer.length !== secretBuffer.length) return false;
    return timingSafeEqual(tokenBuffer, secretBuffer);
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}
```

## 8. In-Depth Project Case Studies & Benchmarks (What production systems has Samir built?)

### Project 1: Production AI Portfolio RAG Chatbot
- **Live URL**: https://samir-portfolio-dev.vercel.app
- **Role**: Creator & Architect
- **Problem Statement**: Standard portfolio websites are passive and force recruiters or clients to search across disparate pages to verify skills, projects, and credentials. Most AI chatbots hallucinate or talk generically without real grounding.
- **Architectural Solution**:
  - Engineered a full RAG retrieval pipeline using Next.js 16 App Router, TypeScript, Neon Serverless PostgreSQL with `pgvector`, Google Gemini `gemini-embedding-2` embeddings, and Groq `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` for streaming chat completions via the Vercel AI SDK.
  - Documents (blogs, projects, experience, resume facts) are parsed into semantic chunks and embedded as 3072-dimensional vectors.
  - Incoming user prompts are embedded and queried against `content_chunks` using `cosineDistance(content_chunks.embedding, queryVector)` with a strict cutoff threshold `<= 0.5`.
  - Database-level filtering via `where(lte(cosineDistance(...), 0.5))` reduces memory pressure before post-processing.
  - Dynamically detects developer-related queries and injects live GitHub activity directly into the context window for real-time proof of work.
  - Zero-hallucination system prompt enforces brevity (1-2 sentences for general queries), prohibits meta-references (never says "according to the context"), and requires exact markdown links (`/about`, `/resume`, `/contact`).
- **Security & Reliability**:
  - Dual-tier rate limiting: In-memory sliding window tracking IP addresses and FingerprintJS visitor IDs (`x-visitor-id`).
  - IPinfo VPN/proxy detection running in fail-open mode.
  - Lightweight `llama-3.1-8b-instant` model routing for follow-up question chip generation to minimize token cost and latency.
- **Performance Benchmarks**:
  - ~10,000 document chunks indexed in PostgreSQL.
  - Vector similarity search latency: <300ms.
  - First token latency (Groq): ~250ms.
  - Hallucination frequency: 0% on verified knowledge facts.

### Project 2: WhatsApp Business Automation Platform
- **Environment**: Active production deployment for a regional SME (automotive/tyre dealership).
- **Role**: Full-Stack Engineer
- **Problem Statement**: The business suffered customer dropouts and delayed inquiries due to manual quote requests, stock lookups, and campaign dispatches.
- **Architectural Solution**:
  - Built a full-stack WhatsApp automation platform — Node.js + Express.js backend with a cross-platform React Native + Expo mobile app for campaign management.
  - Integrated the Google Sheets API as the unified contact and campaign data layer, automating contact/segment synchronization.
  - Engineered QR-based authentication with persistent session recovery to preserve WhatsApp Web connections across restarts.
  - Implemented a concurrency-controlled message queue with configurable delays and rate-limit-aware throttling to respect WhatsApp anti-spam policies while guaranteeing reliable delivery.
  - Added real-time per-contact delivery tracking (send status, failure reasons, retries), media validation, structured logging, and request validation.
- **Impact & Scale**:
  - Actively processing 1,000+ messages per week in production.
  - 0% dropped messages; automated quote turnaround reduced response latency from hours to under 30 seconds.

### Project 3: AI Ticket Triage & Routing System
- **Architecture**: Distributed microservices architecture.
- **Role**: Backend Architect
- **Problem Statement**: High-volume customer support tickets require manual categorization, priority assignment, and routing, creating operational bottlenecks and SLA breaches.
- **Architectural Solution**:
  - Designed an asynchronous event-driven pipeline using Node.js, Express, Apache Kafka, BullMQ, and PostgreSQL.
  - Ingestion service receives incoming support tickets, produces message events onto Kafka topics, and persists raw ticket payloads in PostgreSQL.
  - AI Triage worker consumes messages from Kafka, runs prompt-engineered classification and sentiment analysis via LLM APIs, and generates structured JSON metadata (priority score, department route, required skill tier).
  - Routing worker assigns tickets to queues in BullMQ with priority weighting and dead-letter queue (DLQ) retry semantics.
  - Fully instrumented with OpenTelemetry distributed trace headers passed across service boundaries, publishing metrics to Prometheus and visualizing end-to-end trace latency in Grafana.
- **Impact**:
  - Automated triage of multi-category tickets in <2 seconds.
  - Complete operational visibility into message queue backlog, LLM inference latency, and worker throughput.

### Project 4: Eventify Ticketing Platform
- **Role**: Full-Stack Backend Developer
- **Tech Stack**: GraphQL API, Node.js, PostgreSQL, React, TypeScript.
- **Problem Statement**: Event management and ticketing requires concurrent seat booking, transactional consistency, and secure payment/ticket issuance.
- **Architectural Solution**:
  - Developed a modular GraphQL API using Apollo Server with schema-first definitions.
  - Enforced strict database transactions in PostgreSQL with optimistic locking to prevent double-booking during ticket checkout surges.
  - Integrated Nodemailer for transactional PDF ticket generation and asynchronous delivery.
  - Built Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) separating event attendees, organizers, and superadmins.

### 4-Stage Engineering Delivery Process
- **01 Discovery & Architecture (Day 1–2)**: Understand product goals, data requirements, and technical constraints to define a clear architectural scope and deliverables roadmap.
- **02 Prototype & Validation (Day 2–5)**: Build and validate a working prototype to test core assumptions, AI response quality, and API contracts early with your team.
- **03 Implementation & Hardening (Weeks 1–N)**: Refine business logic, implement caching and error handling, optimize database queries, and test edge cases thoroughly.
- **04 Integration & Handover (Final Day)**: Deploy to production, integrate with existing stack, and provide complete documentation, tests, and code walkthroughs.

## 11. Complete 73-Question FAQ Knowledge Base (AEO Answer Engine Matrix)

### Category 1: Pricing & Payment (Commercial Intent & Risk Mitigation)

#### Q: How much does a freelance project or custom website typically cost?
**A**: A typical freelance project with Samir Shaikh ranges from $300 to $800 (₹25,000 to ₹65,000) for targeted feature sprints and technical SEO audits, and $900 to $2,500+ (₹75,000 to ₹2,00,000+) for complete full-stack web applications or production AI/RAG systems. Every engagement begins with a scope breakdown and a guaranteed fixed-price proposal with no surprise billings.
- *Tags*: Freelance Pricing, Website Cost, Fixed Quote, Next.js Development Cost, AI Project Cost.

#### Q: Do you work with a fixed project budget or hourly rates?
**A**: I work primarily on milestone-based fixed budgets to give clients guaranteed cost certainty and protected timelines. For ongoing product development, continuous engineering roadmaps, or technical advisory, I also provide dedicated weekly retainer sprints ($500 to $900/week) with agreed-upon delivery velocity and daily progress visibility.
- *Tags*: Fixed Budget, Weekly Retainer, Milestone Billing, Contract Pricing, Hourly vs Fixed.

#### Q: What are your payment terms and milestone schedule?
**A**: Payment terms follow a safe 30/35/35 milestone structure tied directly to verified deliverables: 30% upfront deposit to initiate technical architecture and design, 35% upon reviewing working milestone demos on a staging server, and the final 35% only after production deployment, testing sign-off, and repository transfer.
- *Tags*: Payment Terms, Milestone Payments, Safe Escrow, Staging Verification.

#### Q: What if the deliverable does not match requirements or needs revision?
**A**: Every project includes structured revision rounds at each milestone stage to ensure 100% alignment with your expectations. Because we establish concrete technical specifications and UI wireframes before writing production code, scope divergence is caught early. Any deliverable that does not match the agreed specification is revised at zero additional cost.
- *Tags*: Satisfaction Guarantee, Revision Policy, Quality Assurance, Design Review.

#### Q: How much will monthly hosting and database infrastructure cost after launch?
**A**: For most startups and small businesses, monthly infrastructure costs range from $0 to $20/month. Applications are architected on generous modern serverless tiers (Vercel, Neon Serverless PostgreSQL, Cloudinary), ensuring zero payment for idle compute and scaling costs strictly as user traffic and business revenue grow.
- *Tags*: Hosting Costs, Infrastructure Cost, Serverless Architecture, Neon PostgreSQL, Vercel.

#### Q: Why should I invest in a custom Next.js website instead of WordPress or Wix?
**A**: A custom Next.js web application delivers sub-second load times (95+ Google PageSpeed score), zero recurring plugin subscription vulnerabilities, and superior search engine visibility. #### Q: I'm a non-technical founder — can you translate my business idea into a working product without me understanding the code?

I translate business objectives into clear technical specifications using plain-language milestone documents, visual wireframes, and Loom video walkthroughs at every stage. You review working demos on a staging URL — no code review required, ever.

**A**: Hiring a freelance engineer gives you direct access to the senior engineer writing your code — not a project manager who relays specs to a junior team offshore. This means faster decisions, lower overhead cost (typically 40–60% less than agencies), zero account management layers, and a single accountable professional who understands your full technical stack from day one.
- *Tags*: Freelancer vs Agency, Direct Engineering Access, Cost Comparison, Senior Developer, No Middleman.

### Category 4: AI & RAG Systems (Deep Technical Architecture & AI-Enabled Workflow)

#### Q: How is your production RAG pipeline designed and what prevents hallucination?
**A**: My production RAG architecture pairs Google Gemini 3072-dimensional embeddings (`gemini-embedding-2`) with Neon Serverless PostgreSQL and pgvector for sub-300ms vector retrieval. Hallucinations are prevented through strict cosine distance filtering (<= 0.5), deterministic system prompts that enforce verified citations, refusal guardrails when context is insufficient, and real-time activity grounding.
- *Tags*: RAG Pipeline, pgvector, Gemini Embeddings, Hallucination Defense, Vector Search.

#### Q: How do you use AI coding assistants without compromising code quality or security?
**A**: I use AI coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) strictly for repetitive boilerplate, test fixtures, and initial scaffolding — never for unverified production logic. Every line of code passes through strict manual architecture review, unit testing, and automated CI gates, ensuring zero 'AI slop', zero security vulnerabilities, and clean, maintainable software.

The solution features automated document chunking, vector indexing, streaming responses, rate limiting, and seamless embeddable drawer UI widgets tailored to your brand.
- *Tags*: Custom AI Chatbot, Knowledge Base AI, SaaS AI Integration, Streaming UI, RAG Chatbot.

#### Q: Why hire a custom AI engineer instead of using off-the-shelf chatbot software?
**A**: Building a custom AI application gives you 100% proprietary data ownership, zero recurring monthly per-message or per-seat markups, and complete flexibility to connect directly into your internal databases and APIs. Off-the-shelf tools lock your data onto third-party servers and charge steep subscription fees.
- *Tags*: Custom AI vs SaaS, Cost Reduction, Data Sovereignty, API Integration.

#### Q: How do you protect against runaway LLM API bills and high token costs?
**A**: I implement multi-layered cost safeguards: in-memory and IP-based rate limiting, strict token budgets, compact prompt compression, and vector query caching. By pairing cost-effective models (Groq LLaMA 3.3, Google Gemini) with local pgvector retrieval, LLMs only process concise, verified context chunks rather than entire document dumps.
- *Tags*: AI Token Costs, API Billing Safeguards, Rate Limiting, Groq LLaMA, Cost Optimization.

#### Q: How do you choose the right AI model (GPT-4, Gemini, Claude, LLaMA) for a specific use case?
**A**: Model selection is driven by four factors: task complexity (reasoning depth vs. pattern matching), latency requirements (streaming chat vs. batch processing), cost per token at production scale, and data privacy constraints (cloud-hosted vs. locally-hosted open-source models). For most production RAG and chatbot applications, I recommend a hybrid: Gemini embeddings for retrieval with Groq-hosted LLaMA 3.3 for fast streaming inference — delivering sub-second responses at a fraction of GPT-4 costs.
- *Tags*: AI Model Selection, GPT-4 vs Gemini, LLaMA 3.3, Groq, Model Comparison, LLM Cost Optimization.

#### Q: Can you build an AI assistant that securely queries our internal PostgreSQL database or CRM in natural language?
**A**: Yes, I build secure Text-to-SQL and database querying AI agents using read-only database roles, parameterized query generation, and strict schema isolation. The system converts user questions into validated SQL queries, validates execution plans, prevents dangerous write operations, and formats the output into interactive tables and charts with verified data provenance.
- *Tags*: Text to SQL, Database AI Assistant, Internal CRM AI, Read-Only SQL Agent, PostgreSQL Agent, Data Analysis AI.

#### Q: How do you measure and benchmark the accuracy of a custom RAG pipeline?
**A**: I evaluate RAG accuracy using systematic benchmarking frameworks (such as RAGAS metrics) focusing on three core criteria: Faithfulness (is the answer strictly grounded in retrieved context?), Answer Relevancy (did it address the user query without fluff?), and Context Recall (did vector search retrieve the required chunks?). Any drop in evaluation score triggers chunking refinement, threshold tuning, or prompt guardrail updates.
- *Tags*: RAG Evaluation, RAGAS Metrics, Faithfulness Score, Vector Search Quality, RAG Benchmarking, LLM Evaluation.

## 13. Technical Glossary & Terminology Index (Semantic GEO Signals)

- **Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)**: Architecture combining informational retrieval from an external vector index with an LLM prompt to synthesize accurate, verifiable responses without fine-tuning.
- **pgvector**: Open-source vector similarity search extension for PostgreSQL supporting L2 distance, inner product, and cosine distance across high-dimensional embeddings.
- **Cosine Distance (`<=>`)**: Geometric metric evaluating the angle between two embedding vectors. In 3072d space, a distance `<= 0.5` corresponds to high semantic similarity.
- **HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World)**: Multi-layer graph index for approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) vector search providing logarithmic query latency.
- **IVFFlat (Inverted File Flat)**: Inverted index clustering vectors into Voronoi cells; trades slight recall accuracy for reduced memory footprint.
- **Deterministic AI Agent**: An autonomous system utilizing function calling and tool execution where external state mutations are strictly governed by validated JSON schemas (e.g. Zod).
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: Open standard enabling AI models to interact with local development tools, databases, and contextual servers safely.
- **Prompt Injection Defense**: Multi-layered defensive design isolating untrusted user input and retrieved context using structural delimiters, role boundaries, and input sanitization.
- **Bounded Context**: Domain-Driven Design (DDD) pattern isolating a software domain's ubiquitous language, private relational schema, and business rules within explicit boundaries.
- **Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ)**: Queue holding messages or worker jobs that repeatedly fail execution, isolating anomalies without blocking active pipeline consumers.
- **Cache-Aside Pattern**: Caching strategy where application code queries the cache first; on a cache miss, data is read from the database, written to cache with a TTL, and returned.

---

## 15. Legal Information

### Privacy Policy
**URL**: https://samir-portfolio-dev.vercel.app/privacy-policy

This portfolio website collects minimal personal data limited to:
- **Contact form submissions**: Name, email address, and message content — used solely to respond to enquiries. Not sold, shared, or used for marketing.
- **Google Analytics 4**: Anonymised, aggregate usage data (pages visited, time on page, referral source, browser/device type). No personally identifiable information is linked to analytics data. Opt-out available via [Google Analytics Opt-out Add-on](https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout).
- **Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights**: Aggregate page views and real-user Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS). Cookie-free, no persistent cross-site identifiers, no cross-site tracking, and no behavioural profiling. Custom events are limited to the route visited, 75% scroll depth, contact form submission, and AI assistant open. Message content, name, email address, and device fingerprint are never sent to either service. Governed by the [Vercel Privacy Policy](https://vercel.com/legal/privacy-policy); opt out by blocking the measurement script with a content blocker.
- **Server logs (Vercel)**: Standard HTTP request data (IP, path, user agent, timestamp) retained and managed by Vercel for security and reliability purposes.

**Cookies set on public pages**: `_ga`, `_ga_*` (Google Analytics, 2-year / 24-hour expiry). Theme preference stored in localStorage (no personal data). Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights set no cookies. No advertising or cross-site tracking cookies are set anywhere on this site.

**Private admin area**: `/admin` sets a strictly necessary authentication session cookie (`authjs.session-token`, or its `__Secure-` variant) for administrators only. It is not used for visitor tracking and is not shared with third parties.

**Third-party data processors**:
- Vercel — hosting and edge infrastructure, plus Web Analytics and Speed Insights measurement
- Neon (Serverless PostgreSQL) — contact form database storage
- Google Analytics — anonymised usage analytics
- Cloudinary — image and media hosting

**Data retention**: Contact form submissions retained until the enquiry is resolved. GA data retained for 14 months (Google's default). Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights data retained in aggregate form on a rolling 90-day window, never against an individual visitor.

**User rights**: Right to access, correct, or delete personal data submitted through this site. Contact: shaikh.samir.work@gmail.com with subject "Data Request". Response within 30 days.
